title: Sentence Structure
description: Learn to build correct English sentences and avoid common errors.
competenceGoals: use central patterns for pronunciation, vocabulary and sentence structure

content.content:
# Sentence Structure

English sentences follow specific patterns. Understanding these patterns helps you
write correctly and avoid common Norwegian-English errors.

content.title: Basic Word Order
content.content:
English uses **SVO** order: Subject - Verb - Object

- **Subject**: Who/what does the action
- **Verb**: The action
- **Object**: Who/what receives the action

*"**The cat** (S) **caught** (V) **a mouse** (O)."*

content.title: Adverb Placement
content.content:
## Where to Put Adverbs

**Frequency adverbs** (always, never, often, usually) go BEFORE the main verb:
- *"I **always** eat breakfast."*
- *"I eat always breakfast."* (incorrect)

But AFTER the verb "be":
- *"She **is always** happy."*
- *"She always is happy."* (incorrect)

content.title: Common Norwegian-English Errors
content.content:
**Don't translate directly from Norwegian!**

"I like me to play football." - "I **like** to play football."

"It is many people here." - "There **are** many people here."

"I have lived here in three years." - "I have lived here **for** three years."

"I am agree." - "I **agree**." (no "am")

content.title: Question Formation
content.content:
## Making Questions

**Yes/No questions**: Put auxiliary verb first
- Statement: *"She **can** swim."*
- Question: ***"Can** she swim?"*

**Wh-questions**: Wh-word + auxiliary + subject + verb
- ***"Where** does she live?"*
- ***"What** are you doing?"*

**Important**: Don't forget the auxiliary (do/does/did)!
- *"Where she lives?"* (incorrect)
- *"Where **does** she live?"* (correct)

content.title: Do/Does in Questions
content.content:
In present simple questions, use **do/does** + base verb:
- *"**Does** she **like** pizza?"* (not "Does she likes")
- *"**Do** you **play** football?"*

The main verb stays in base form - don't add -s!

exercise.task: Which sentence has correct word order?

subTasks.label: a
subTasks.task: Identify the sentence with correct adverb placement.

exercise.solution: Frequency adverbs come before the main verb.

subTasks.label: a
subTasks.solution: What time does the train leave?
multipleChoiceOptions: What time does the train leave?

exercise.solution: It follows the pattern: Wh-word + does + subject + base verb.

exercise.task: Fix this Norwegian-English error: "I have lived here in five years."

subTasks.label: a
subTasks.task: Correct the preposition error in this sentence.
subTasks.solution: I have lived here for five years.
multipleChoiceOptions: I have lived here for five years.
I have lived here since five years.
I lived here in five years.
I am living here in five years.

exercise.solution: Use "for" with periods of time (five years, two hours, etc.).

exercise.task: Correct the errors in these sentences.

subTasks.label: a
subTasks.solution: "I like to read books." (remove "me" - this is a Norwegian pattern)
multipleChoiceOptions: "I like to read books." (remove "me" - this is a Norwegian pattern)
"I am liking me to read books."

subTasks.label: b
subTasks.task: "It is many students in my class."
subTasks.solution: "There are many students in my class." (use "there are" for existence)
multipleChoiceOptions: "There are many students in my class." (use "there are" for existence)
"It are many students in my class."
"Many students it is in my class."

subTasks.label: c
subTasks.solution: "Where does she live?" (base verb after does, no -s)
multipleChoiceOptions: "Where does she live?" (base verb after does, no -s)

hints: Think about what sounds natural in English
exercise.solution: Recognizing common errors helps you avoid them in your own writing.
